items.title: Somalia national intelligence agency abducts journalist reporting on security tensions in Mogadishu
items.description: At midday on Sunday, plainclothes NISA officers abducted journalist Khadar Abdirahim Ibrahim of Himilo Media in Mogadishu, according to his colleagues. items.title: Famine risk grows in southern Somalia as food crisis deepens
items.description: Emergency-level conditions are expected in parts of Bay, Bakool and Hiiraan, as well as riverine areas and settlements for internally displaced people. items.title: Somalia: Xawaadle Elders and Al-Shabaab Reportedly Reach Truce in Hiiraan
items.description: A 16-point joint statement circulated by Al-Shabaab-affiliated media  said the sides had resolved their disputes and agreed to maintain peace in areas controlled or influenced by the clan. The reported agreement includes a commitment by Hawadle elders not to allow the recruitment or operation of Macawiisley fighters in their areas or provide them with shelter. Macawiisley forces from Hiiraan have played a key role in supporting Somali government troops against Al-Shabaab. The meeting in Maxaas was attended by dozens of traditional elders, while Al-Shabaab was represented by senior figures
items.titleIt: Somalia: Xawaadle Elders and Al-Shabaab Reportedly Reach Truce in Hiiraan

items.description: Residents reported hearing a series of powerful explosions across Baidoa, with thick plumes of smoke visible over parts of the city. items.description: The Federal Government of Somalia and the United Nations warn that projected flooding and funding shortfalls could worsen the hunger crisis and push more people – especially children -- into extreme food insecurity and acute malnutrition.   The latest Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC)* analysis projects that 5.4 million people will face crisis levels of hunger or worse between October and December 2026, including 1.5 million people facing emergency levels of hunger or worse. items.title: Ten Years On, Somalia's Lower Shabelle's Farmers Still Can't Go Home: A Decade of War, Land Disputes, and Aid That Never Reaches Far Enough
items.description: It was the latest wave in a displacement crisis that has been building in Somalia's Lower Shabelle region for a decade, and there is no sign it is reversing. Aadan Rooble knows the pattern well. He walked for part of the ten days it took him to reach Mogadishu after airstrikes made the decision for him — the farm his family worked in the village of Farxaano was no longer somewhere anyone could stay. His sons now find casual work when they can. He doesn't expect to go home. He's one of tens of thousands of farmers who have fled Somalia's Lower Shabelle region over the past decade, arriving in M
items.titleIt: Ten Years On, Somalia's Lower Shabelle's Farmers Still Can't Go Home: A Decade of War, Land Disputes, and Aid That Never Reaches Far Enough

items.description: The boat went down during the night of Oct. 8-9 near Guehere, north of the port town of Obock. The shipwreck is among the deadliest recorded on the Eastern Route, a migration corridor used by people traveling from the Horn of Africa toward Yemen and other destinations in the Arabian Peninsula. items.titleIt: Death toll rises to 139 after migrant boat capsizes off Djibouti
